newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 11.0/11.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 11.0/11.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 11.0/11.5 percent on Friday morning on steady liquidity.
Dealers said liquidity was sufficient on the back of central bank injection of 394 billion rupiah.
One local bank dealer said longer-term rates were also lower, with one-week money softening to 12.0 percent and one-month money to 13.0/13.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 13.87 percent, compared with 16.51 percent on Tuesday.
Bond dealers said the market remained well bid, with prices seen edging up by some 25 to 50 basis points late on Wednesday.
They said focus was still on the 500 billion rupiah seven-year straight bond of Bank DKI with a fixed coupon of 15.5 percent for the first year.
